text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 ALERT 1735551234 - High p99 latency and streaming stalls observed for /v1/stream.generate in us-west-2. p99 ~12s, p95 ~1.2s, ~11% of streams stalled or timed out. Paging on-call SREs: marta, lee.

marta: I'm on call. pulling perf dashboard and recent logs. starting timeline.

lee: seeing the same in traces — heavy tail from kv-cache misses then long stall at accel layer. p99 tail correlates to a small set of GPU nodes (gpu-uw-11..13).

sam: just got an alert from node-monitor: repeated ECC correctable errors on gpu-uw-12, and thermal throttle events on gpu-uw-13. NVML shows increasing correctable ECC counts.

tina: Support: two paying customers reported streaming stalls, one timed out on a 30s client wait -> returned 504. CS flagged severity. Andre, fyi.

andre: copying SEs, customers asking if this is widespread. Please include customer lists in the incident notes.

marta: quick triage plan: 1) isolate affected GPU nodes 2) reroute new streaming sessions off those nodes to warm spares 3) enable CPU fallback for long-running streams where acceptable 4) capture nvml and kernel logs for postmortem.

lee: agree. I'm going to bump routing weight away from us-west-2 GPU pool by 70% and enable fallback model variant for streaming: redwood-stream-small-quantized. That should reduce load.

sam: draining gpu-uw-12 now to stop new allocations:
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-uw-12
kubectl drain node/gpu-uw-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

sam: drain confirmed, pod eviction started. moving existing streams: we'll gracefully proxy in-progress streams to fallback if possible.

lee: routing change applied: `route-manager set-weight us-west-2/gpu-pool -70% && route-manager add-fallback redwood-stream-small-quantized`

incident-bot: AUTO: Routing policy change detected by deploy-bot at 1735551402.

deploy-bot: Rollout: routing change to add fallback model applied to us-west-2 (canary 5% -> 100%). No config errors detected.

marta: checking hardware logs from gpu-uw-12: excerpt:
```
[kernel] Correctable ECC error on GPU 0, count +3
[nvml] Thermal throttle engaged: GPU 0 temperature rose to 90C
[nvml] ECC corrected errors incremented
```

lee: that lines up. Correctable ECC + thermal can cause periodic stalls while driver retries memory operations. Might explain the long tail.

sam: running `nvidia-smi --query-ecc-errors=single_bit_double_bit --format=csv` shows spikes on gpu-uw-12 and gpu-uw-13 in the last 10 minutes.

marta: immediate mitigations in flight: - drained gpu-uw-12 - cordoned gpu-uw-13 pending thermal probe - scaled up gpu-spare-pool by 3 instances - temporary circuit-breaker lowered to 25 concurrent streaming requests per node in us-west-2

lee: monitoring shows p99 dropping from ~12s to ~3.2s after drain + routing change. p95 now ~750ms. Still above target for some customers, but trending better.

incident-bot: NOTE: SLO alert still firing (p99 > 2s) for streaming.generate in us-west-2.

tina: CS update: affected customers = [AcmeCorp, BrightApp]. Acme reported one failed critical call. Tina will open ticket and offer credits if confirmed impact.

andre: please add severity tag and timeline for each affected customer. I'll start outreach drafts.

marta: collecting core dumps and driver logs. Please capture `dmesg`, `kern.log`, and `nv-hostengine.log` from the drained nodes.

sam: logs uploaded to /infra/incident_logs/1735551234/ (NVML, dmesg, container logs).

lee: hypothesis: a flaky DIMM on gpu-uw-12 triggers correctable ECC bursts, driver retries lead to stalls, thermal events then push driver into conservative clocks causing longer latency; fallback hits reduce pressure.

marta: plan for next steps: 1) keep nodes cordoned 2) run stress tests on spare hardware to reproduce ECC/thermal pattern 3) schedule hot-swap of gpu-uw-12 (maintenance window) 4) postmortem to include memory ECC counts and kernel patches if any.

sam: I've filed a hardware ticket with cloud provider for gpu-uw-12/13 with attached ECC logs. Support ref: #CL-98122.

lee: for immediate customer protection I'm going to extend fallback routing to 100% for any new long-running streaming sessions in us-west-2 for the next 30m. That should reduce tail load.

marta: agreed. Also enabling more aggressive kv-cache TTLs and prefix-caching to reduce cache miss storms that amplify tail.

incident-bot: METRIC SNAPSHOT 1735551600 - before mitigations: p99=12.4s p95=1.2s error_rate=11.2% after initial mitigations: p99=3.2s p95=0.75s error_rate=2.8%

tina: CS: Acme confirmed one 504; open support case 7892. We're coordinating a customer patch note: degraded performance briefly for streaming in us-west-2.

andre: send the outreach to Acme now with ETA for full resolution. We should also offer a follow-up call.

marta: status update: draining finished on gpu-uw-12, hardware flagged for replacement. gpu-uw-13 remains cordoned pending thermal hardware probes. Scaling and fallback kept active.

lee: traces show no new long stalls after routing bump; tail appears limited to older sessions pinned to impacted nodes. We should be able to close P1 once p99 < 1.5s sustained and error_rate < 1% for 30m.

sam: provider confirmed scheduled maintenance window for replacement in 2 hours. We'll keep nodes out of rotation until healthy.

marta: action items assigned: marta -> incident lead & postmortem; lee -> tracing & perf regression check; sam -> hardware ticket & logs; tina/andre -> customer comms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 1735552400 - p99=1.4s p95=0.55s error_rate=0.9% (30m rolling). Condition for CLOSE met.

marta: moving to P2 / recovery state. Leaving measures in place (fallback + cordons) until replacement complete. Will draft postmortem and timeline.

lee: will follow up with quantized-model quality check to ensure fallback didn't regress outputs for critical customers.

tina: CS will notify customers that mitigation completed and share postmortem when available.

marta: closing notes: root causes likely hardware-level ECC bursts and thermal throttling on two GPUs; contributing factor: sudden cache miss pattern amplified load on small subset of nodes. Postmortem will include timeline, mitigation decisions, and long-term remediation (auto-quarantine on ECC spikes, earlier thermal ramp detection).

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED 1735552800 - Status: mitigated, owners assigned for postmortem.

marta: thanks team. filing next steps and slack log into the incident ticket. :thumbsup:

lee: nice work. I'll attach traces and a short rerun script to repro in staging.

sam: hardware ticket updated with follow-up and logs.

andre: I'll follow up with customers after the postmortem.

tina: marking support cases as incident-impacted and adding credit recommendation draft.

marta: end of thread.
